\extable{300_q37_t1}

A person with a taxable income of \$90 000 pays $25.8\%$ of that income in tax (excluding any levies).

What is the value of $X$ in the table?

solutions.latex:
Tax on $\$90\,000$ is $25.8\%$ of the income.
$$\$90\,000\times 0.258 = \$23\,220$$
The income above $\$78\,800$ is taxed at $X$ cents per dollar.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Income over } \$78\,800 &= 90\,000-78\,800\\ &= \$11\,200\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Tax on this part} &= 23\,220-18\,292\\ &= \$4928\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}11\,200\times X &= 4928\\ X &= \dfrac{4928}{11\,200}\\ &= 0.44\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ X = 44 \text{ cents}$$
criteria: Finds the amount to which $X$ cents applies, or equivalent merit

\extable{36_q20_t1}

For the 2019–2020 financial year, Wally had a taxable income of \$122 680. During the year, he paid \$3000 per month in Pay As You Go (PAYG) tax.

Calculate Wally's tax refund, ignoring the Medicare levy.

solutions.latex:
Tax payable from the table:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Tax} &= 20\,797 + 0.37(122\,680 - 90\,000) \\ &= \$32\,888.60 \end{aligned}$$
PAYG tax paid:
$$3000 \times 12 = \$36\,000$$
Refund:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Refund} &= 36\,000 - 32\,888.60 \\ &= \$3111.40 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Provides correct calculation of tax, or equivalent merit
Makes some progress towards calculating the tax payable, or equivalent merit

\extable{15_q33_t1}

Marcus earned an annual gross salary of \$109 200 and had allowable deductions of \$8700.

Calculate Marcus's total tax payable, including the Medicare Levy which is charged at 2% of taxable income.

solutions.latex:
Taxable income is gross salary less deductions.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Taxable income} &= 109\,200 - 8700 \\ &= \$100\,500 \end{aligned}$$
From the tax table, income tax payable is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Income tax} &= 5092 + 0.325(100\,500 - 45\,000) \\ &= \$23\,129.50 \end{aligned}$$
The Medicare levy is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Medicare levy} &= 2\% \times 100\,500 \\ &= \$2010 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total tax payable} &= 23\,129.50 + 2010 \\ &= \$25\,139.50 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct taxable income and income tax payable, or taxable income and Medicare levy, or correct tax payable with one mistake, or equivalent merit

\extable{38_q22_t1}

William has a gross annual salary of $\$84\,000$. He has allowable tax deductions of $\$900$ for home-office equipment and $\$474$ for union fees. William must also pay a Medicare Levy of 2% of his taxable income.

Calculate the total tax payable by William including the Medicare Levy.

solutions.latex:
Taxable income is gross salary less deductions.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Taxable income} &= 84\,000 - 900 - 474 \\ &= \$82\,626 \end{aligned}$$
Income tax payable, using the tax table:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Income tax} &= 5092 + 0.325\times(82\,626 - 45\,000) \\ &= \$17\,320.45 \end{aligned}$$
Medicare levy:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Medicare levy} &= 0.02\times 82\,626 \\ &= \$1652.52 \end{aligned}$$
Total to be paid:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= \$17\,320.45 + \$1652.52 \\ &= \$18\,972.97 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates income tax payable, or equivalent merit
Calculates taxable income, or equivalent merit
